reasoning: According to records from the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and historical budget data, the last time Congress passed all of its regular annual appropriations bills on time (before the October 1 deadline marking the start of the fiscal year) was for Fiscal Year 1997 (which was enacted in late September 1996). Since then, Congress has not passed a complete federal budget on time, relying instead on a combination of continuing resolutions (CRs) and omnibus spending packages passed after the deadline to maintain government operations.
